message: What's really fun is seeing Cicero apply his rhetorical theory in the orations. The *Pro Milone*, *In Catilinam*, *Pro Caelio*, and *Pro Ligario* are all absolutely masterful. It seems to me that Cicero is all about rhetoric, and the politics that accompany rhetoric, while Quintilian is all about education -- and, as an imperially-appointed "chair" of rhetoric in an age when you had to be very careful about speaking out, he *didn't* much talk about politics.
